Title: Update your NVIDIA graphics driver
Why: NVIDIA GPU drivers are not delivered reliably through Windows Update. Fresh drivers fix game crashes, improve performance, and patch security issues — so it's best to get them straight from NVIDIA.
Steps: Click "Open official page" below to go to NVIDIA's driver download site.
Pick your product type (GeForce), series, and exact GPU model, then your Windows version.
Download the latest Game Ready Driver (or Studio Driver if you do creative work).
Run the downloaded installer and choose "Express" installation.
Restart your PC if it asks, then come back and mark this guide as done.
AppSteps: Click "Open NVIDIA App" below — it launches the NVIDIA App you already have.
Click "Check for updates", then download the latest driver.
Choose "Express installation" and let it finish.
Restart if asked, then mark this guide as done.

Title: Update your AMD Radeon graphics driver
Why: AMD Radeon drivers often arrive late or incomplete through Windows Update. The official AMD package (Adrenalin) brings the newest fixes, game optimizations, and security patches.
Steps: Click "Open official page" below to go to AMD's support site.
Use "Search" or the product selector to find your exact Radeon model.
Download the recommended Adrenalin Edition driver for your Windows version.
Run the installer and choose the recommended (Express) installation.
Restart your PC if asked, then mark this guide as done.

Title: Update your Intel graphics driver
Why: Intel integrated graphics drivers from your PC maker can lag behind. Intel's own driver adds the latest stability and performance fixes — though on some laptops the maker's version is required, so update via your laptop maker if Intel's installer warns you.
Steps: Click "Open official page" below to open Intel's Download Center.
Search for "Graphics" and pick the driver matching your Intel graphics (e.g. Iris Xe / UHD).
Download the latest installer (.exe) for your Windows version.
Run it; if Intel says your PC maker customized the driver, get it from your laptop maker instead.
Restart if asked, then mark this guide as done.

Title: Update Visual Studio workloads
Why: Visual Studio's own workloads and components aren't managed by winget or Windows Update — they only update through the separate Visual Studio Installer.
Steps: Open the Start Menu and launch "Visual Studio Installer".
If an update is available, click "Update" next to your Visual Studio edition.
To add or update specific workloads, click "Modify" instead and check the workloads you want.
Let the installer finish, then restart Visual Studio if it asks.
Come back and mark this guide as done.
AppSteps: If an update is available, click "Update" next to your Visual Studio edition.
To add or update specific workloads, click "Modify" instead and check the workloads you want.
Let the installer finish, then restart Visual Studio if it asks.
Come back and mark this guide as done.

Title: An updated app won't open and asks for .NET
Why: Sometimes an app you just updated moves to a newer .NET and then refuses to open with a message like "To run this application, you must install .NET". The fix is quick: install the exact .NET Desktop Runtime version it names. Each major version installs side by side, so this never breaks your other apps.
Steps: Read the error window carefully — it names the exact version it wants (e.g. ".NET 8.0") and usually offers a download link.
Click "Open official page" below and pick that same major version from the list.
Under "Run desktop apps", download the ".NET Desktop Runtime" installer for Windows x64 (x86 only if the app is 32-bit).
Run the installer and let it finish — no restart is usually needed.
Open the app that was failing again — then mark this guide as done.

Title: Problems right after a GPU driver update? Clean-reinstall (DDU)
Why: If you get black screens, flickering, artifacts, or crashes right after updating your GPU driver (from the Drivers page or the guides here) — or a driver install that keeps failing halfway — leftover files from old drivers are the usual culprit. Display Driver Uninstaller (DDU) is the free community-standard tool that strips the old driver completely so a fresh one installs cleanly.
Steps: FIRST download the fresh driver for your GPU (NVIDIA/AMD/Intel guides above) — after cleaning you'll have no driver and a basic-resolution screen.
Click "Open official page" below and download the latest Display Driver Uninstaller (DDU) from Wagnardsoft.

Disconnect from the internet (so Windows can't auto-install its own driver mid-clean), then restart into Safe Mode: Start → Power → hold Shift while clicking Restart → Troubleshoot → Startup Settings.
In Safe Mode run DDU, pick your GPU type, and choose "Clean and restart".
After the restart, run the fresh driver installer you downloaded in step 1, reconnect to the internet, and mark this guide as done.
